To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the interpersonal influence network is the same as the network describing the relation of agents’ initial opinion for successive issues, (ii) the connectivity of the interpersonal influence network implies the existence of opinion clusters over issue sequences in the F–J dynamics, and (iii) opinion consensus is achieved over issue sequences in a social network if the connectivity of the corresponding interpersonal influence network is preserved.
the interpersonal influence network is the key to understanding the opinion evolution in the F–J models.
the F–J opinion dynamics model with stubborn agents is convergent over issue sequences if and only if the interpersonal influence network is connected.

the opinion formation of the stubborn agents over issue sequences can be analyzed in a systematic way by taking advantage of the network structure of interpersonal influence and the relationship of agents' initial opinions for successive issue sequences.
